name: Museum of Arts and Design
_poi_role_reasoning: A single multi-floor museum building with described interior studios, a discrete stop.
_poi_role_source: MAD offers four floors of superlative design and handicrafts

beats.script_body: The Museum of Arts and Design, known as MAD, holds some 2,000 items in its permanent collection alone, including objects of fashion, design, and jewelry. There is more than enough here to give you a sense of how craft, ornament, and everyday objects become art.
beats.source_passage: The Museum of Arts and Design (MAD) has some 2,000 items in the permanent collection alone, including objects of fashion, design, and jewelry.

beats.script_body: MAD is also known for its radical building renovation, which was not very well received in the architecture world. Particularly controversial were the windows, which appear to spell out the word "hi." Look up at the facade on Columbus Circle and judge for yourself. On the flip side, diners in the ninth-floor restaurant have an excellent view of Central Park.

physical_cues.cue: Facade windows that appear to spell out the word "hi" on Columbus Circle
Ninth-floor restaurant with a view of Central Park

beats.script_body: Many famous people have stayed at the Plaza Hotel. Architect Frank Lloyd Wright, for example, stayed here while he was designing the Guggenheim. Rooms on the north side of the hotel have a great view of Central Park, and if you're not dressed too shabbily you can probably steal a peek into the lobby.

name: Museum of Modern Art
short_description: World-class art museum, very high tourist gravity.
_poi_role_reasoning: A discrete museum destination, trigger_radius 25m, beats describe standing before specific artworks.
_poi_role_source: Van Gogh's Starry Night, its thick brush strokes visible in person

beats.script_body: The world-famous Museum of Modern Art, MoMA, holds an extensive and unique collection of contemporary and modern art. There is plenty to see, from a helicopter suspended from the ceiling and a collection of old computers to artwork by Picasso and modern video art. Don't forget to also visit the MoMA Design Store.

physical_cues.cue: Helicopter suspended from the ceiling inside the galleries

beats.script_body: Learn all about the history of radio and television at the Paley Center for Media. Here you can watch and hear a Frank Sinatra concert, re-experience the first Star Trek episode, or settle in for a documentary, all drawn from the center's broadcasting archive.

beats.script_body: 21 Club stands for all the history and stories that make New York so fantastic. Since 1930, "The 21" has been an institution for "everyone who is anyone," made clear by the enormous number of artifacts donated by famous people over the years. The jockey statues on the facade are proud gifts from Jay van Urk, the Vanderbilts, and many other notables.

name: St. Patrick's Cathedral
short_description: Largest Roman Catholic cathedral in the US; distinct from existing 'Old St. Patrick's Cathedral' in SoHo.
_poi_role_reasoning: A discrete cathedral building with front spires and Tiffany altar, a single destination.
_poi_role_source: The cathedral filling an entire city block at Fifth Ave and 51st St

beats.script_body: The impressive St. Patrick's Cathedral, built in 1879, is the largest Gothic cathedral in the United States and can seat more than 2,000 people. Be sure to look for the Tiffany altars, the stained-glass windows, and the Pieta, the statue of Mary holding the body of Jesus.

name: Rockefeller Center
short_description: Multi-block complex (Top of the Rock, rink, Radio City); high gravity.
_poi_role_reasoning: A several-blocks-wide complex of 19 buildings you walk through following 'The Channel', trigger_radius 60m.
_poi_role_source: The several-blocks-wide collection of 19 buildings forming an airy, light space

beats.script_body: In 1928, John D. Rockefeller bought a piece of property that he developed into office buildings and public promenades. He called it Rockefeller Center. Come here in winter to go ice skating next to the giant Christmas tree, and don't pass up a trip to 30 Rockefeller Plaza and the observation deck, Top of the Rock, with its unobstructed view of Central Park and the Empire State Building.

physical_cues.cue: Winter ice rink beside the giant Christmas tree
Top of the Rock observation deck at 30 Rockefeller Plaza, with views of Central Park and the Empire State Building

You also won't want to pass up a trip to 30 Rockefeller Plaza and the observation deck, Top of the Rock, where you have an unobstructed view of Central Park and the Empire State Building.

name: Radio City Music Hall
short_description: Art Deco theater, Rockettes / Christmas Spectacular; part of Rockefeller area.
_poi_role_reasoning: A discrete theater building you stand at, trigger_radius 25m; not nested under a candidate_parent (Rockefeller Center is in this batch but containment handled separately).
_poi_role_source: The exquisite Art Deco features of the music hall's interior

beats.script_body: One of the most popular events at Radio City Music Hall is the "Christmas Spectacular" with performances by the Rockettes. Radio City Music Hall is the largest covered theater in the world and a beautiful example of art deco style.

name: Times Square
short_description: Most congested pedestrian icon in the Western Hemisphere; very high gravity.
_poi_role_reasoning: A large pedestrianized square you cross and stand within, framed as an area covering many surrounding buildings rather than a single point.
_poi_role_source: Costumed characters and 'painted ladies' roaming the pedestrianized square

beats.trigger_address: Broadway and 7th Avenue between 42nd and 47th streets
beats.script_body: With its bright lights, enormous billboards, and constant crowds, Times Square is the pulse of New York City. Under the red stairs you'll find the TKTS Booth, where you can buy discounted tickets, sometimes up to 50 percent off, for shows on and off Broadway and for dance and music performances. Go early, because the lines can be long.

beats.script_body: Take a trip to the International Center of Photography to see unique photos from around the world. There are always plenty of good temporary exhibits on view here.

name: New York Public Library
short_description: Beaux Arts main branch (Stephen A. Schwarzman Building) with lion statues.
_poi_role_reasoning: A single Beaux Arts building you stand before, marked by the lions Patience and Fortitude at the entrance.
_poi_role_source: The famous stone lions guarding the entrance

beats.script_body: The largest branch of the New York Public Library opened in 1911 and is housed in the Stephen A. Schwarzman Building. In the 1930s, Mayor Fiorello LaGuardia gave the marble lions sitting outside the building the nicknames Patience and Fortitude. In doing so, he was emphasizing the very qualities New Yorkers needed to endure the Depression.

physical_cues.cue: Marble lions Patience and Fortitude flanking the steps outside the building

name: Bryant Park
_poi_role_reasoning: A 4-acre park with 120m radius and promenade framing; a contextual area you walk through, and itself a candidate parent.
_poi_role_source: a 4-acre lawn surrounded by benches, statuary, and London planetree–shaded promenades

beats.script_body: Head to Bryant Park for some rest and relaxation. Grab a coffee and a snack at one of the kiosks, then sit back and take in the tall buildings around you. At the east edge of the park is one of the city's most popular outdoor bars, and in summer there are open-air movies every Monday night. Until 2010, New York Fashion Week was also held here twice a year, before it moved to Lincoln Center.

physical_cues.cue: Refreshment kiosks and lawn surrounded by tall buildings

name: Grand Central Terminal
short_description: Major Beaux Arts transit landmark, Frommer's 'best historic building'. High gravity.
_poi_role_reasoning: A single landmark transit building with facade and interior cues you stand before, not an area walked through.
_poi_role_source: Beaux Arts interior of Grand Central, restored to its original brilliance

beats.trigger_address: 89 E 42nd St between Madison and Lexington avenues
beats.script_body: Grand Central Terminal is a Beaux Arts masterpiece that embodies the romanticism of train travel. Its annual Holiday Laser Light Show, a Christmas-themed display projected onto the ceiling of the main hall, begins on November 30 and runs for six weeks. It is very impressive.

physical_cues.cue: Ceiling of the main hall, surface of the Holiday Laser Light Show

name: Chrysler Building
short_description: Iconic Art Deco skyscraper, named by Frommer's as best NYC skyscraper and New Yorkers' favorite. High-gravity landmark.
_poi_role_reasoning: A single iconic skyscraper you look up at; cues describe standing before one object despite the moderate radius.
_poi_role_source: Sleek Art Deco hood-ornament spire of the Chrysler Building

beats.script_body: The Chrysler Building is the crowning achievement of auto-industry giant Walter P. Chrysler. Designs of hubcaps and fenders are worked into the building inside and out, and you'll find waterspouts shaped like radiator caps. The 1,046-foot art deco monument opened in 1930 as the tallest building in the world, only to be dethroned one year later by the Empire State Building.

physical_cues.cue: Hubcap and fender motifs and radiator-cap-shaped waterspouts on the facade

beats.source_passage: The Chrysler Building is the crowning achievement of auto industry giant Walter P. Chrysler. Designs of hubcaps and fenders have been incorporated into the building both inside and out. You'll also find waterspouts in the shape of radiator caps. The 1,046-foot-tall (319 meters) building is a unique art deco monument. When it opened in 1930, the Chrysler Building was the tallest building in the world. One year later, it was dethroned by the Empire State Building.

name: The Morgan Library & Museum
short_description: J.P. Morgan's library; Gutenberg Bibles, rare manuscripts.
_poi_role_reasoning: A discrete museum building you stand before, with interior cues like the East Room and Gutenberg Bibles.
_poi_role_source: Incorporating the mansion once owned by financier JP Morgan, this sumptuous cultural center

beats.script_body: The wonderful collection at The Morgan Library & Museum came from the private holdings of wealthy banker and art collector John Pierpont Morgan. In 1924, eleven years after his death, it was opened as a public institution. The collection includes manuscripts, drawings, books, and old Middle Eastern tablets, among other things.

name: Empire State Building
short_description: Iconic global landmark, top observation deck, very high tourist gravity.
_poi_role_reasoning: A discrete iconic building you stand at and ascend, trigger_radius 40m, tier 5.
_poi_role_source: The view of Manhattan from the observation deck, 1,454 feet up

beats.script_body: The Empire State Building was the result of a race between the chairmen of General Motors and Chrysler to see who could build the world's tallest building first; General Motors "won." The pencil-shaped tower opened in 1931 and, until 1971, was indeed the tallest building in the world. The view from the 86th floor is as phenomenal as ever.

physical_cues.cue: View from the 86th-floor observation deck

name: Flatiron Building

_poi_role_reasoning: A single iconic building you stand before, trigger_radius 30m.

beats.script_body: The Flatiron Building was designed in 1902 in an attempt to establish a new business district north of Wall Street, and it sits perfectly on a triangular, iron-shaped plot of land. It's usually windy around the iconic building, so be sure to hold on to your hat.

name: Gramercy Park
_poi_role_reasoning: A park-and-surrounding-square area (radius 120) you walk around viewing the bordering homes and clubs, a contextual area.
_poi_role_source: Around it, beautifully preserved historic homes and clubs include the wisteria-clad home

beats.trigger_address: Between 20th and 21st streets and Park and 3rd avenues
beats.script_body: Gramercy Park is the only non-public park in New York; only residents living in the area hold a key. In the 19th century most apartments here were intended for the poor, so the apartments at 34 Gramercy Park East were called "French flats" to set them apart from the working-class buildings nearby. Go for a drink on the beautiful terrace of the Gramercy Park Hotel.

beats.script_body: The Union Square Greenmarket began in 1976 with a handful of farmers and has grown into an enormous market where some 140 regional farmers come to sell their products in peak season. Vendors offer organic fruits and vegetables, bread, cheese, and organic wine, and you can catch cooking demonstrations from famous local chefs and sample their creations.

physical_cues.cue: Market stalls along the north and west sides of Union Square

In the winter the market is somewhat smaller. Vendors sell organic fruits and vegetables, bread, cheese, and organic wine. Be sure to also check out the cooking demonstrations from famous local chefs and sample their creations.
